exception.reason: UCR provides substantive comparative law, human rights, criminal justice, public international and European law, constitutional/administrative law, private law and transnational business law. These contributions are preserved. They do not establish the target-defining sustained progression in Dutch doctrinal legal analysis across foundational and advanced contracts, property, family, employment, company law, civil/insolvency procedure and criminal procedure, integrated Dutch legal-source/argumentation methods, pleading and independent legal research. PrivateLaw explicitly compares primarily Germany, France, England, China andUSA; its selected private-lawfields do not supply the complete Dutch civil-lawsequence. General rhetorical advocacy, negotiation, organisationalpsychology, socialresearch, AIbusinessanalysis and climate/earthscience cannot stand in for that missing disciplinary substance. The first proposal contains8law-focused7.5ECcourses60EC, leaving120ECincompanions; the climateproposal has7lawfoundation/trackcourses52.5EC, withscience/media/governancecompanions. Those companions can be coherent but do not provide the defining legal depth. Alternative technology/climate topics are legal applications within a lawdegree, not evidence that climate science alone supplies climate law. This is a substantive academic no-match, independent of professionalqualification/automaticmasteradmission. A law-and-societyprogramme could be valuable but is a different target.

audience.programmeDescription: VU Law develops legal reasoning across Dutch private, criminal, constitutional and administrative law, European and international law. Students learn to interpret legal sources, solve cases, argue in writing and speech, and progress to advanced doctrinal study, pleading and independent legal research.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers substantive study of comparative law, human rights, criminal justice, public international and European law, private law and business law. These courses do not form a complete programme with the sustained Dutch doctrinal progression and integrated legal methods, procedure and research that define this degree. We therefore show the verified VU curriculum without presenting a UCR programme as a comparable alternative.

curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC pathway comprises 150 EC of compulsory legal study and 30 EC of open minor or approved study. PPI 1, PPI 2 and Dutch language testing are integrated credit or grade requirements. Thesis entry requires 120 EC including Legal Skills; pleading requires 99 EC including Legal Skills. Course prerequisites, attendance and open-study approval rules apply.
